variants.original: Run heavy, the ground packs hard: so much steadiness nothing new can root, stillness sealed into immobility. Till the field. Even bedrock is improved by weather.

variants.candidate: With too much Wood, the roots draw more than the ground can feed, and the slope gives way under the trees it carries. Turn down the next demand and rest a week.

variants.candidate: With too much Fire, the soil bakes to a hard dry crust over the seed, and nothing planted in it comes up. Make one thing from all you took in and hand it over.

variants.candidate: With too much Metal, the hill is hollowed out by its own ore, every thought coming out finished and pointed while the ground under it thins. Keep one opinion back and sleep on it.
